question.text: If $P$ be a point on the parabola $y^{2}=4 a x$ with focus $F$. Let $Q$ denote the foot of the perpendicular from $P$ onto the directrix. Then, $\frac{\tan \angle P Q F}{\tan \angle P F Q}$ is

solution.text: Equation of parabola is $$ y^{2}=4 a x $$ Let the parametric coordinate of point $P$ on the parabola is $(a, 2 a)$ Now. $Q F=2 \sqrt{2} a$ $$ P Q=2 a \text { and } P F=2 a $$ we observe that, $O F^{2}=P Q^{2}+P F^{2}$ $\Rightarrow \quad 8 a^{2}=4 a^{2}+4 a^{2}=8 a^{2}$ So, $\Delta Q P F$ form a right angle isoceles triangle. In which, $\angle P Q F=\angle P F Q$ $\Rightarrow$ $\tan \angle P Q F=\tan \angle P F Q$ $\Rightarrow$ $\frac{\tan \angle P Q F}{\tan \angle P F Q}=1$
